synthesis: The source presents two bridge constructions for the same global functional limit: truncated Euler products obtain fixed-test variance and negative-Sobolev/Wasserstein control by matching full, mixed, and truncated two-point kernels, while finite Dirichlet polynomials replace the difficult mixed Euler-product kernel by easier finite cross moments but do not retain comparably good control of truncated-Euler-product approximation errors.
source_support: Units u018-u020 derive full, mixed, and truncated kernel asymptotics, combine them into omitted-Z-mass variance control, and lift scalar estimates through Fourier probes to a nested negative-Sobolev mean-square and Wasserstein approximation. Unit u022 closes the global limit by a three-edge triangle through a fixed Euler truncation. Unit u023 explicitly offers finite Dirichlet polynomials as a route that bypasses the mixed two-point estimates, reproduces the approximation architecture using finite Z,A sums, and warns that this route appears less able to yield good error estimates for truncated Euler products.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis compares the choice of intermediate representation as a proof-engineering tradeoff: an Euler-product bridge requires the harder mixed-kernel estimate but exposes quantitative variance and function-space control, whereas a finite-polynomial bridge simplifies the cross-moment step while weakening the available error information.
limits: Both constructions are alternative derivations of the same randomized limit, not independent evidence for its law. The source says good truncated-Euler-product errors appear harder to obtain by the alternative argument; it does not prove that every finite-Dirichlet-polynomial approximation rate is strictly worse. Constants in the finite-set estimates may depend on A, the function-space conclusion uses nested truncation/height limits and alpha greater than one half, and exact formula symbols remain extraction-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted because distinct units jointly establish a concrete substitution of bridge object, its downstream effect on the proof mechanism, and an explicit quantitative limitation. The relation is stated by the source's alternative-proof remark and becomes visible only by connecting the kernel, variance, Sobolev-lift, limit-triangle, and finite-polynomial units; it is neither a generic shared theme nor a paraphrase-only combination.
